newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian government denies pyramid scheme funding.
newsitem.headline: Albanian government denies pyramid scheme funding.

text.p: Albania's ruling Democratic Party on Tuesday rejected as "vile slander" an opposition party charge that it had used money from pyramid schemes to finance its election campaign last year.

The centre-right Democratic Alliance Party (DAP) had earlier alleged that President Sali Berisha's Democrats had misused funds invested by Albanians in such schemes -- which have mushroomed in Europe's poorest country -- for its own benefit.
"It is a vile slander characteristic for the Democratic Alliance Party that these firms financed the campaign of the Democratic Party (DP)," DP's public relations chief, Arben Cejku, told Reuters.

Get-rich-quick schemes promising returns of up to 50 percent a month have been proliferating in Albania for several years and have drawn hundreds of millions of dollars, sending alarm bells ringing at international financial institutions.

The DAP, set up by a group of dissidents who fell out with the ruling Democrats soon after they came to power in a landslide victory over the Socialist Party in March 1992, said the pyramid schemes were destined to collapse and slammed the accumulation of vast sums of money outside the banking system.

Cejku said the conservative Democratic Party had obtained its share of campaign money from the state budget, in line with an Albanian law which allocates funds for political campaigning based on the parties' share of parliamentary seats.
The Democrats increased their representation to 122 seats in the 140-member monocameral parliament in the Balkan nation's disputed parliamentary elections on May 26 and June 2.

The Socialists, the DAP and most other opposition parties pulled out of the elections, alleging that the Democrats rigged the vote. The Socialists have stuck to their decision not to take up their 10 seats in parliament.

Cejku said the Democratic Party's parliamentary group had sponsored the creation of a special committee which is scheduled to start looking into the activities of pyramid schemes on Friday, to secure more transparency in the process.
"The Democratic Party has neither encouraged nor prohibited the creation of these private organisations and their clients have cooperated with them on a private basis," he added.
